title: A Vow for the Orchard
premise: Beatrix Vane returns to her family's failing orchard estate for a reunion that doubles as an inheritance trial: whoever proves they can 'sustain the Vane legacy' within a year claims the land. Desperate to deflect her scheming cousins, she recruits Elias Thorne, a guarded hotelier with his own family wreckage, to pose as her boyfriend. Their fake romance deepens even as Beatrix discovers the inheritance clause was engineered by her grandmother to force the family to confront how their fortune was built on a betrayal. In the end, Beatrix refuses the inheritance on those terms, Elias forgives himself for his brother's ruin, and the two plant a new orchard together on leased ground — choosing love and honest work over corrupted legacy.
about_author: August Coldharbour is the pen name of a former orchard hand who spent fifteen years writing in farm kitchens before turning to romance. Known for moody coastal settings and heroes who must earn their tenderness, Coldharbour writes about families that are equal parts shelter and storm.

chapters.title: The Summons in the Salt Air
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A lawyer's letter arrives at her lighthouse cottage: the Vane reunion will decide the orchard's inheritance, and attendance is mandatory. Beatrix, stalled on her second novel and broke, dreads facing cousins who mock her 'little stories.' Emotional beat: dread sharpened by stubborn pride as she packs for a home that never felt like one.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Gatehouse
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Checking into the inn he nearly bought, Elias overhears Beatrix arguing on the phone about needing a date. Impulsively — or perhaps fleeing his own empty suite and his brother's lawsuit — he offers himself. She assumes he's joking; he isn't. Emotional beat: two lonely people mistaking recklessness for relief.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Over cider in the inn's kitchen, they negotiate rules: no real names of exes, no touching unless required, leave after dessert. Beatrix invents a meet-cute; Elias corrects it with something truer than fiction. Emotional beat: playful banter curdling slightly when both realize they're rehearsing intimacy they've forgotten how to perform.

chapters.title: The Reunion Table
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The first reunion dinner: cousin Marcus performs devotion to Grandmother Vane while quietly courting developers; Aunt Rosalind interrogates Elias like a customs officer. Beatrix's hand finds Elias's under the table — breaking rule three. Emotional beat: the fake date starts feeling load-bearing.

chapters.title: What the Orchard Remembers
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Wandering the orchard at dawn, Elias finds Beatrix reading her grandmother's old ledgers, which hint the Vane fortune came from a swindled business partner. He recognizes the pattern — his own father did the same. Emotional beat: kinship through inherited guilt, and the first unguarded conversation between them.

chapters.title: Rain on the Glasshouse
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Storm traps them in the derelict glasshouse; a kiss happens that breaks every rule. Afterward Beatrix panics, insisting it was 'for the cousins.' Elias, hurt, almost walks — until Marcus offers him money to spy on Beatrix. Emotional beat: desire colliding with self-protection; the fake begins to cost real things.

chapters.title: The Clause in the Will
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix deciphers the full inheritance clause: the winner must sustain the legacy 'as founded' — meaning publicly confessing its rotten origin. Grandmother Vane engineered the whole trial as penance. Meanwhile Elias accepts Marcus's retainer, telling himself he'll never use it. Emotional beat: revelation and quiet betrayal running on parallel tracks.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Marcus exposes Elias's payments at the harvest gala, framing him as a hired con. Beatrix's public humiliation becomes his mirror moment: he sees his father's opportunism in himself. He confesses everything — the money, the brother's lawsuit, the shame. Emotional beat: climax of self-forgiveness begun by choosing truth over advantage.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. At the final judgment, Beatrix stands before the family and refuses the poisoned inheritance, reading her grandmother's ledgers aloud and proposing the orchard become a cooperative trust. Marcus storms out; Rosalind, unexpectedly, stays. Elias arrives soaked from the rain to stand beside her. Emotional beat: catharsis — legacy redefined as accountability, not possession.

chapters.title: Second Chances, Better Timing
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, closing with Elias's letter read aloud. One year later: the trust thrives, Beatrix's novel — about a lighthouse keeper and a liar who learned honesty — is finished, and Elias has leased the neighboring field. They plant saplings where the old betrayal took root. Emotional beat: resolution as renewal; love chosen freely, timing finally right.
